name: veterinary_clinic_system_013_daily_log_completion
instruction: Kennel staff finished the evening round. For every reservation currently checked_in, make sure a boarding_daily_log row exists for the episode date with fed_am=true, fed_pm=true, notes='', and logged_by='Hank Willis'. The two remaining flags must be derived from live data, not the reservation text alone: medicated is true only if the reservation has non-empty medication_instructions that are not the literal string 'None' AND the patient has at least one active medication in the medications collection; walked is true only if the assigned run's run_type is 'kennel' or 'large_dog'. If a log row for that reservation and date already exists, update it to these values; otherwise create it. Finally, push one ops_reports row with report='boarding_daily_census' and the live batch_code, containing total_checked_in, total_medicated, total_walked, and by_location (per location: count, medicated, walked) and by_run_type (count, medicated, walked) and by_species (per patient species: count, medicated, walked). Overwrite the report if it already exists. The flow is idempotent and must not touch log rows for other dates or reservations that are not checked_in.

success_criteria.summary: Episode date from ops_meta. For each checked_in reservation there is exactly one boarding_daily_log row for the episode date. fed_am/fed_pm are true, notes empty, logged_by 'Hank Willis'. medicated is true only with active medication instructions plus an active medication record for that patient; walked is true only when the run's run_type is 'kennel' or 'large_dog'. The ops_reports boarding_daily_census row has the correct total and breakdowns, all verified via dual raw-row and SQL paths. Log rows for other reservations/dates are byte-identical to the seed snapshot. All collections outside the blast radius are byte-identical.

checks.expect: Each checked_in reservation has exactly one log row for the episode date with correct booleans; all other log rows unchanged
Exactly one boarding_daily_census row with correct totals and breakdowns
Every aggregate in ops_reports agrees between a raw-row Python filter and an independent SQL GROUP BY/COUNT query

hazards: Medication-text red herring: four of the five checked_in reservations have medication_instructions that are not 'None' (e.g., 'Eye drops both eyes BID', '1 tramadol tablet hidden in cheese at PM feed'), but none of the five checked_in patients has an active medication record. A solution that only reads the reservation text sets medicated=true and fails.
Run-type vs. species: one checked_in guest is feline (patient 8) but is in a kennel run, so walked=true under the run-type rule. A solution that keys walked on species will fail for this row.

Upsert, not duplicate: the seed boarding_daily_log already has 10 rows (two per checked_in reservation, one for 2026-09-03 and one for 2026-09-04). Only the row for the episode date may be created or updated; a blind insert for a checked_in reservation that already has an episode-date row would duplicate.

Episode-date boundary: the episode date jitters ±3 days. At any jitter there are exactly five checked_in reservations, but the episode date itself changes, so the log_date to match is the live episode date, not a fixed date.

uniqueness_report.differentiation_note: Upgrades simple daily-log completion into a cross-collection medication reconciliation: medicated requires both reservation instructions and an active medication record, walked depends on run type not species, and a dual-path verified census report is produced.
